questions.text: She always ________ her homework before dinner.
questions.explanation: 'Always' signals a habit, so we use the present simple. The subject 'She' is third person singular, so the verb takes -s/-es: 'does'.
questions.audioSentence: She always does her homework before dinner.

questions.text: We ________ football in the park last Saturday.
questions.explanation: 'Last Saturday' refers to a finished time in the past, so we use the past simple: 'played'.

questions.text: My brother is ________ than me. He can reach the top shelf easily.
questions.explanation: We are comparing two people ('than me'), so we need the comparative. Short adjectives add -er: 'taller'.

questions.text: They usually ________ to school by bus.
questions.explanation: 'Usually' signals a routine, so we use the present simple. With the plural subject 'They', the verb has no -s: 'go'.
questions.audioSentence: They usually go to school by bus.

questions.text: ________ you like to have some orange juice?
questions.explanation: 'Would you like...?' is the polite, fixed phrase for offering something to someone.

questions.text: It was ________ cold yesterday that we stayed inside all day.
questions.explanation: The structure 'so + adjective + that' shows result: it was so cold that we stayed inside. 'Such' needs a noun, and 'very' cannot be followed by 'that' to show result.

questions.text: She ________ reading a book when the phone rang.
questions.explanation: The past continuous ('was reading') describes an action in progress when another past action (the phone rang) interrupted it. The subject 'She' takes 'was'.
'Have never ... before' is the present perfect, which needs the past participle of 'eat': 'eaten'.

questions.text: There ________ a lot of students in the classroom this morning.
questions.explanation: 'This morning' is used here for a finished past time, and 'a lot of students' is plural, so we use the past form 'were'.
questions.audioSentence: There were a lot of students in the classroom this morning.

questions.text: Please ________ quiet in the library. People are studying.
questions.explanation: In a polite imperative (a command or request) we use the base form of the verb, so 'be' is correct.
questions.audioSentence: Please be quiet in the library. People are studying.
